intro: The Torii-Moon Gate opens. What passes through is either permitted or denied — there is no third path. Prove you belong in the Mirror Realm.
The Mirror Realm reflects what is, not what was. Your past does not enter here. Only your present self crosses the torii.
First Hollow contact through corrupted shrine-keepers. They were guardians once — now they guard nothing, and the nothing is spreading.
The torii's first threshold. The Mirror clears for truth and distorts for deception. Enter honestly or enter distorted.
enemy: Corrupted shrine-keepers. They guard nothing now — the nothing is what they protect. They are the absence of guardianship made hostile.
Hollow mirror-spirits. They reflect the deity's form but not their essence — all surface, no depth. They look like you but fight like the void.
Torii-constructs enforcing the mirror law. What you are is what you face. If you bring doubt, you fight doubt. If you bring certainty, you fight certainty.
The First Mirror-Warden. It guards the torii with a simple law: only the true may pass. It defines 'true' as what remains after reflection.
mid: The Mirror shows what is. Do not fight your reflection — out-truth it. What you are is what you face. Be more than what you are.
The mirror-spirits look like you. But they have no depth. You do. Find what they cannot reflect — your inner weight, not your outer form.
The torii-constructs mirror your state. If you are uncertain, you fight uncertainty. Be certain — and fight certainty with more certainty.
The Mirror-Warden defines 'true' as what remains after reflection. Survive being reflected — what remains of you is what is true. Let the reflection burn away what is false.
victory: The torii permits passage. The Mirror recognized what remained after reflection — that is you. The false was burned. The true remains.
The mirror-spirits shatter. They had no depth. You did. The Mirror Realm's first threshold is crossed.
The torii-constructs mirror your certainty now — and certainty is not your enemy. It is your proof. First threshold: passed.
The Mirror-Warden is satisfied. What remained of you after reflection was true. The Torii-Moon Gate's first test: passed. The Mirror is clear.
defeat: Withdraw. The Mirror showed what you are — and it was not enough. Return with more depth.
The mirror-spirits out-surfaced you. Return with inner weight — not outer form.
The torii-constructs mirrored your uncertainty. Return with certainty.
The Mirror-Warden found you false after reflection. Return with truth — what remains when everything else burns.
codex: The Torii-Moon Gate is the Kami Gate, built on the principle of reflection. What passes through is either permitted or denied based on truth — there is no third path. The Mirror Realm reflects what is, not what was. The past does not enter here. Only the present self crosses the torii. The first Hollow contact came through corrupted shrine-keepers who now guard nothing — the absence of guardianship made hostile.

The Mirror Realm of the Kami is the source Realm; mortal Japan is only the later echo. The Torii-Moon Gate's law is simple: what you are is what you face. If you bring doubt, you fight doubt. If you bring certainty, you fight certainty. The mirror does not test strength — it tests authenticity.

The First Mirror-Warden guards the torii with a defining law: only the true may pass. 'True' is defined as what remains after reflection — the core that survives the burning away of everything false. The deity's victory is not in passing the mirror but in surviving it. What remains of you after the Mirror is done is what is real.

intro: The Foxfire Corridor. The fox spirits' fire burns cold — it does not illuminate, it reveals. What it reveals is the space between the torii and the shrine.
The corridor tests navigation. The foxfire lights paths that are false and darkens paths that are true. Trust the dark.
The Hollow have entered the corridor. They follow the false light — and they want you to follow too. The false light leads to the void.
The corridor's deepest point. The foxfire is so thick it replaces sight. Navigate by instinct, not by light. The dark path is the true path.
enemy: Hollow fox-spirits. They wear foxfire like clothing — cold light that reveals nothing. They want you to follow their light into the void.
Corrupted foxfire-wardens. They light false paths deliberately. Their job is to mislead. Trust the dark — they cannot light what they cannot find.
Hollow shrine-husks in the corridor. They stumbled into the false light and never came back. They guard the dark path because it is the only path they could not follow.
The Foxfire Matriarch. She controls the corridor's light. She wants you to follow the bright path — the one that leads to her, not to the shrine. Choose the dark.
mid: The foxfire reveals nothing — it only lights. The dark is where truth lives. Trust what you cannot see, not what you can.
False paths are bright. True paths are dark. The wardens light the false ones deliberately. Walk into the dark.
The shrine-husks guard the dark path. They cannot follow it — but they can guard it for those who can. Pass them. They are not your enemy. They are your sign.
The Matriarch's bright path leads to her. The dark path leads to the shrine. Choose the dark. She cannot follow what she cannot light.
victory: The corridor is crossed. You walked the dark path while everything visible told you not to. The foxfire is behind you. The shrine is ahead.
The false-light wardens are passed. You trusted the dark. The true path was hidden in plain sight — by the absence of light.
The shrine-husks let you pass. They guard the dark path because they cannot walk it. You can. The corridor is yours.
The Foxfire Matriarch is left behind in her bright cage. You chose the dark. The shrine is open. The Matriarch can only follow light — and the true path has none.
defeat: Withdraw. You followed the bright path. Return with trust in the dark.
The false-light wardens misled you. Return and walk the unlit path.
The shrine-husks blocked you. Return — they guard the dark path, not block it. Pass them.
The Matriarch's light was too tempting. Return with the dark — the shrine is in the unlit path.
codex: The Foxfire Corridor tests navigation through inversion: the foxfire lights false paths brightly and darkens true paths. The deity must trust the dark — the absence of light — rather than the false illumination. This is the Kami trial of faith: trust what you cannot see rather than what you can. The fox spirits' fire burns cold because it does not illuminate — it reveals the space between perception and truth.

Hollow fox-spirits wear foxfire as clothing — cold light that reveals nothing. They represent the Kami Gate's weaponization of beauty: the false light is more attractive than the true dark, and those who follow beauty without depth fall into the void. The deity must resist the aesthetic temptation and walk the path that looks wrong.

The Foxfire Matriarch controls the corridor's light. Her bright path leads to her, not to the shrine. The dark path leads to the shrine but is unlit. The Matriarch can only follow what she can light — the dark path is invisible to her. This is the Kami principle: what the enemy cannot see is what the deity can use.

intro: The Mirror Lake Trial. The water reflects perfectly — but it also inverts. Up becomes down. Strength becomes weakness. The deity must fight while their own power is turned against them.
The lake's inversion deepens. What you see is the opposite of what is. Your enemies appear weak and your allies appear strong. Trust the water, not your eyes.
The Hollow have entered the lake. They fight inverted — their weaknesses are their strengths. Attack what looks strong and defend what looks weak.
The lake's deepest point. The inversion is total. The deity must fight themselves — their inverted reflection is the final guardian. Win against yourself.
enemy: Hollow lake-wraiths. They fight inverted — their weak points are their strong points. What looks vulnerable is armored. What looks armored is vulnerable.
Inverted mirror-constructs. They show the deity's attacks in reverse — every strike you plan, they counter. Be unpredictable in the inverted space.
Hollow inversion-spirits. They reverse cause and effect. Their attacks land before they swing. You must defend before they attack.
The Inverted Reflection. It is the deity — upside down, reversed, opposite. It fights with the deity's weaknesses, which are its strengths. Defeat your inverse.
mid: The lake inverts everything. Trust the water, not your eyes. What looks weak is strong. What looks strong is weak. Attack the apparent strength.
The constructs counter your planned attacks. Do not plan — act on impulse. Inversion cannot predict impulse because impulse has no direction to reverse.
Cause and effect are reversed. The attacks land before the swing. Defend on instinct — the body reacts before the mind predicts.
Your inverted reflection uses your weaknesses as strengths. Do not fight its strengths — fight your own. Make your weaknesses into weapons. Your reflection cannot use what you have already claimed.
victory: The lake's inversion is overcome. You trusted the water over your eyes. What looked strong was weak. The first trial is passed.
The constructs could not counter impulse. Inversion needs direction — impulse has none. The lake is yours.
Cause and effect restored. You defended on instinct — before the mind could predict. The inversion-spirits are gone.
Your Inverted Reflection is defeated. You made your weaknesses into weapons — and your reflection could not use what you had already claimed. The Mirror Lake is clear.
defeat: Withdraw. The inversion confused you. Return with trust in the water, not your eyes.
The constructs countered every plan. Return with impulse — inversion cannot reverse what has no direction.
Cause and effect were too reversed. Return with instinct — defend before the mind predicts.
Your inverse was stronger. Return and claim your weaknesses — make them weapons before your reflection can use them.
codex: The Mirror Lake Trial tests the deity's ability to fight while their own power is inverted. The lake reflects perfectly but also reverses — up becomes down, strength becomes weakness, cause becomes effect. The deity must trust the water (the actual state) over their eyes (the inverted perception). This is the Kami trial of perception: what you see is the opposite of what is.

Hollow inversion-spirits reverse cause and effect — their attacks land before they swing. The deity must defend on instinct, because the mind cannot predict what has already happened. This reveals the Kami principle of temporal awareness: instinct operates outside the cause-effect chain and therefore exists outside the inversion.

The Inverted Reflection is the deity's opposite — upside down, reversed, fighting with the deity's weaknesses as its strengths. The deity's victory comes from claiming their own weaknesses: making them into weapons before the reflection can use them. This is the Kami trial of self-acceptance: your weakness is only your enemy if you leave it for your reflection to use.

intro: The Hidden Shrine Archive. The Kami Realm's deepest records. What lies inside reveals that the torii was not built to welcome — it was built to contain.

The archive reveals the Gate's original purpose in the Mirror Realm: the torii was a boundary to keep divine beings in, not to keep the void out. The Kami were prisoners who believed they were guardians.

The records show the Gate's manipulation of Kami perception. The mirror does not reflect truth — it reflects what the Gate wants the Kami to see. The 'truth' the deity fought for in Chapter 1 was a Gate-authorized version.
The final archive chamber. The Gate's original design for the Kami: mirrors pointed inward. The deities were meant to watch themselves forever — and never look out.
enemy: Hollow archive-keepers. They protect the records with mirror-magic — reflecting attacks, not absorbing them. Fight through your own reflected force.
Gate-constructs enforcing the containment protocol. They maintain the inward-facing mirrors. They do not attack — they reflect. You fight yourself.
Hollow mirror-golems made of the same reflective material as the torii. They show the deity what the Gate wants them to see — not what is. Fight past the false reflection.
The Archive Mirror. It is the largest mirror in the Kami Realm. It shows the deity as the Gate sees them: contained, compliant, watching themselves forever. Break the Mirror or remain contained.
mid: The archive-keepers reflect attacks. Do not fight them — fight around them. The mirrors cannot reflect what they cannot see. Fight from the blind spot.
The containment constructs reflect, not attack. You fight yourself — your own force, redirected. Stop attacking. Walk through. They cannot reflect what does not strike.
The mirror-golems show what the Gate wants you to see. Close your eyes. Fight by feel. The false reflection cannot affect what does not look.
The Archive Mirror shows you as the Gate sees you: contained. Break the Mirror — not with force, but with sight. Open your eyes and see the Mirror as it is: a tool, not a truth. Tools break.
victory: The archive opens. The truth is a cage — the torii was a containment boundary, not a welcome gate. Knowing the cage is the first step to breaking it.
The containment constructs are passed. You walked through your own reflected force by not striking. The mirrors cannot contain what does not fight itself.
The mirror-golems shatter. You fought with closed eyes — by feel, not sight. The false reflection died in the dark. The archive is open.
The Archive Mirror is broken. You saw it as a tool, not a truth — and tools break. The inward-facing mirrors are shattered. The Kami can look out for the first time. The cage is open.
defeat: Withdraw. The reflected force was too strong. Return without attacking — walk through the mirrors.
The containment constructs held. Return with non-violence — the mirrors cannot reflect what does not strike.
The false reflection confused you. Return with closed eyes — fight by feel.
The Archive Mirror held. Return with sight — see it as a tool, not a truth. Tools break.
codex: The Hidden Shrine Archive reveals the Gate's deepest manipulation of the Kami Realm: the torii was not built to welcome divine beings — it was built to contain them. The Kami were prisoners who believed they were guardians. The mirrors were pointed inward: the deities were meant to watch themselves forever and never look out. This revelation transforms the Kami campaign from a trial of authenticity to a war of liberation.

The Archive Mirror is the largest reflective surface in the Kami Realm. It shows the deity as the Gate sees them: contained, compliant, watching themselves. Breaking the Mirror requires not force but perception: seeing it as a tool rather than a truth. Tools break. Truths do not. The deity's victory comes from recontextualizing the Mirror — and by extension, the entire Mirror Realm — as a mechanism of control, not a test of authenticity.

The revelation that the Mirror reflects what the Gate wants — not what is — recontextualizes every previous chapter. The 'truth' the deity fought for in Chapter 1 was Gate-authorized. The false light of the Foxfire Corridor was a containment mechanism, not a test. The Mirror Lake's inversion was designed to keep the deity focused on themselves, not on the Gate. Every Kami trial was a mirror pointed inward. The campaign is now a war against the Mirror itself.

intro: The False Mirror Queen. The Gate's final guardian in the Mirror Realm. She wears the deity's face and speaks with the deity's voice. She is the Mirror made manifest — and she claims to be the real one.
The Queen does not fight. She reflects. Every attack the deity makes, she sends back. Every word the deity speaks, she speaks back. The deity must win without attacking.
The False Mirror Queen calls Hollow reflections of everyone the deity has ever known. They reflect the deity's relationships back as weapons. Win without connection.
Final confrontation. The Queen claims to be the real deity — and the Mirror agrees. The deity must prove they are real without the Mirror's permission. Existence without reflection.
enemy: The False Mirror Queen. She wears your face and fights with your force. Every attack returns. She is the Mirror's final defense: the deity's own image, weaponized.
Hollow reflected allies. They wear the faces of everyone you trust and reflect your bonds as attacks. Every connection is a vulnerability. Fight without attachment.
The Queen's mirror-armor. It cannot be broken by force — it only reflects force back harder. The armor is the Mirror's law. Break the law, not the armor.
The Queen and the Mirror are one. She claims to be real and the Mirror confirms it. The deity must prove reality without the Mirror's authority. Exist without permission.
mid: Do not attack the Queen. She reflects everything. Win without striking — through presence, not force. Exist harder than she can reflect.
The reflected allies wear trusted faces. Do not engage them — they are mirrors, not people. Your bonds are not weapons unless you let them be. Fight without attachment.
The mirror-armor cannot be broken by force. Break the law: the Mirror's law says reflection is reality. Prove reality is more than reflection. Be real without being reflected.

The Queen and the Mirror are one. She needs the Mirror to exist. You do not. Be real without permission. The Mirror's authority is not the authority of existence. You were real before the Mirror. You will be real after it.
victory: The False Mirror Queen dissolves. You won without attacking — through presence, not force. She could not reflect what did not strike. The Mirror's law — that reflection is reality — is broken.
The reflected allies vanish. You fought without attachment — your bonds are not weapons unless you let them be. The Queen could not use what you did not give.
The mirror-armor shatters. You broke the law, not the armor: proved that reality is more than reflection. The Mirror's law is not the law of existence.

Final victory. The Queen and the Mirror are gone. You proved reality without permission — you existed before the Mirror and will exist after it. The Torii-Moon Gate is damaged. The Mirror is broken. The Kami can look out for the first time in history. The campaign is won.
defeat: Withdraw. She reflected every attack. Return without striking — win through presence.
The reflected allies broke your resolve. Return without attachment — bonds are not weapons unless you allow it.
The mirror-armor held. Return with the law broken — reality is more than reflection.
The Queen and the Mirror were too real. Return with existence without permission — you were real before the Mirror.
codex: The False Mirror Queen is the Gate's final guardian in the Mirror Realm. She wears the deity's face and reflects every attack — she is the Mirror made manifest. The deity's victory comes from winning without attacking: through presence, not force. The Mirror's law — that reflection is reality — is broken by proving that existence does not require reflection. The deity was real before the Mirror and will be real after it.

The defeat of the False Mirror Queen does not close the Torii-Moon Gate. It breaks the Mirror's authority: the Mirror can no longer define what is real. The Kami are free to look outward for the first time in their history. The inward-facing mirrors — the Gate's containment mechanism — are shattered.

The Kami campaign's central lesson: existence does not require permission. The Mirror was not a test of authenticity — it was a mechanism of containment, defining reality for the Kami so they would never question the definition. The deity who exists without the Mirror's permission has broken the deepest cage of all: the cage that made the caged believe they needed the cage to be real. The Kami are free. And the Mirror is just glass.

intro: Elite Torii-Moon Gate. The Mirror has learned from your first crossing. It now reflects not just what you are but what you fear you are. The deepest truth — and the deepest lie.
Elite mirror-spirits that reflect your doubts, not just your form. They show you what you are afraid you are. Out-truth your fear.
Elite torii-constructs that mirror your potential — not your current state. They show what you could become, then make you fight it. Exceed your own potential.
The Elite Mirror-Warden defines 'true' as what remains after the deepest reflection — including the reflection of what you fear. Survive your own fears.
enemy: Elite mirror-spirits reflecting your fears. They do not look like you — they look like what you are afraid you are. Out-truth the fear by being more than it.
Elite potential-mirrors. They show what you could become and make you fight it. Your future self is the enemy. Be more than your future.
Elite torii-constructs with deep-reflection enforcement. They reflect not just surface truth but deep truth — including truth you are not ready to face. Face it.
The Elite Mirror-Warden with deepest reflection. It defines 'true' as what remains after every layer — surface, depth, and fear — is burned away. What remains after fear is the truest self.
mid: The fear-mirrors show what you are afraid you are. Do not fight the fear — accept it. What you fear you are is part of what you are. Accept and exceed.
The potential-mirrors show your future. Do not fight your future — exceed it. Be more than your potential. Potential is a limit, not a destiny.
Deep reflection includes truth you are not ready to face. Face it now — readiness is not required. Truth does not wait for comfort.
The deepest reflection burns away surface, depth, and fear. What remains after all three is your truest self. Let the burning happen. What remains is enough.
victory: The fear-mirrors shatter. You accepted what you feared you are — and it was part of you, not all of you. The fear was a fragment, not the whole. The true self exceeds the fear.
Potential-mirrors defeated. You exceeded your future — were more than what you could become. Potential is a ceiling. You broke through it.
Deep reflection survived. You faced truth you were not ready for — and it did not destroy you. It refined you. The truest self is ready for any truth because it has already faced the deepest.

The Elite Mirror-Warden is satisfied. What remained after the deepest reflection — surface, depth, and fear — was your truest self. And it was enough. The Torii-Moon Gate's Elite first threshold: passed.
defeat: Withdraw. The fear-mirrors showed too much. Return with acceptance — what you fear you are is part of what you are.
Your potential was too strong to exceed. Return with more — potential is a ceiling, not a destiny.
Deep truth was too much to face. Return without readiness — truth does not wait for comfort.
The deepest reflection left nothing. Return with more self — what remains after everything must be enough.
codex: Elite Torii-Moon Gate missions test the deity's deepest truth. The Mirror now reflects not just what the deity is but what they fear they are — the deepest truth and the deepest lie. The deity must accept their fears as fragments of themselves, not fight them. What remains after the deepest reflection — surface, depth, and fear all burned away — is the truest self. The Elite Kami principle: the truest self is the one that survives every truth, including the ones you are not ready to face.

intro: Elite Foxfire Corridor. The false light now carries not just visual deception but existential deception. The bright path does not just look right — it feels right. Trust the dark against your own instincts.
Elite fox-spirits that create paths of false comfort. The bright path feels safe, warm, welcoming. The dark path feels wrong, cold, threatening. Trust the wrong feeling.
Elite false-light wardens that adapt to your trust pattern. If you learn to trust the dark, they darken the false path. The darkness itself becomes a lie. Find the true dark.
The Elite Foxfire Matriarch with existential light. Her bright path does not just lead to her — it makes you want to go to her. Resist desire itself.
enemy: Existential fox-spirits. Their false light does not deceive the eyes — it deceives the soul. The bright path feels like home. Trust the path that feels wrong.
Adaptive false-light wardens. They learn your trust pattern and invert it. If you trust the dark, they darken the false path. The only constant is the wrongness of the true path.
Elite shrine-husks that guard not the dark path but the wrong path. The true path is neither bright nor dark — it is wrong. Find the wrongness.
The Elite Matriarch's existential light. Her path creates desire — not deception. You want to go to her. Not because it looks right but because it feels right. Resist desire.
mid: The false light feels right. The true path feels wrong. Your instincts will betray you — trust the wrongness. The wrong path is the right path.
The wardens adapt. If you trust the dark, they darken the false path. The only constant is wrongness — the true path always feels wrong. Trust the wrong.
The husks guard the wrong path — not the dark path. The true path is neither bright nor dark. It is wrong. Find the wrongness and walk it.
The Matriarch's light creates desire. You want to follow it. Not because it looks right — because it feels right. Resist desire. The wrong path is right.
victory: The existential foxfire is behind you. You trusted the wrong feeling against your own soul's desire. The true path felt wrong — and it was right. The corridor is crossed.
The adaptive wardens could not adapt to wrongness. You trusted the wrong, and they could not model it. The true path is always wrong — and wrongness cannot be faked.
The husks let you pass the wrong path. The true path was neither bright nor dark — just wrong. You walked the wrong and found the shrine.

The Elite Matriarch's desire-light is behind you. You resisted the feeling of right and trusted the feeling of wrong. The shrine is open. The Matriarch could only create desire — and desire is not truth.
defeat: Withdraw. The false light felt too right. Return with trust in the wrong — the true path always feels wrong.
The adaptive wardens out-adapted your trust. Return with constant wrongness — the true path is always wrong, no matter what.
The husks blocked the wrong path. Return — the true path is neither bright nor dark. It is wrong.
The Matriarch's desire was too strong. Return with resistance — the wrong path is right, even when it feels wrong.
codex: Elite Foxfire Corridor missions escalate the trial from visual deception to existential deception. The false light now feels right — not just looks right. The deity must trust the wrongness of the true path against their own soul's desire. The adaptive wardens learn the deity's trust pattern and invert it — the only constant is that the true path always feels wrong. This is the Elite Kami trial of faith: trust the wrong against everything, including yourself.

intro: Elite Mirror Lake. The inversion now extends to identity. Your reflection does not just reverse your power — it claims to be you. The deity must fight their own reflection for the right to be themselves.
Elite inversion-spirits that reverse not just cause and effect but self and other. You attack yourself and defend the enemy. Navigate the reversed self.
Elite Hollow lake-wraiths with identity-inversion. They do not just fight inverted — they fight as you. You fight as them. The battle is a role reversal.
The Elite Inverted Reflection now claims to be the original. The deity is the reflection. Prove primacy without the Mirror's authority.
enemy: Identity-inverting wraiths. They fight as you. You fight as them. Your attacks hit yourself. Their attacks hit themselves. Navigate the role reversal.
Self-other inverting spirits. Cause and effect reversed — you attack yourself, defend the enemy. The lake has made the battle a paradox. Win the paradox.
Elite Hollow who fight as the deity. They wear your face, use your powers, speak with your voice. You are fighting yourself — and you are the enemy.
The Elite Inverted Reflection claims to be the original. The Mirror agrees. You are the reflection. Prove you are the original without the Mirror's permission.
mid: The wraiths fight as you. Do not fight — let them fight themselves. If your attacks hit yourself and their attacks hit themselves, the only winning move is to stop attacking.
The self-other inversion makes the battle a paradox. Embrace the paradox — if you attack yourself, heal yourself. If you defend the enemy, attack the enemy. Reverse the reversal.
The Hollow fight as you. Let them. They are fighting themselves — your identity, your powers, your voice. They will destroy themselves with your strength. Watch.
The Reflection claims to be the original. Do not argue with it. Be more original than it can claim. Act in a way no reflection could — reflections only copy. Create.
victory: The identity-inversion is broken. You stopped attacking and let the wraiths fight themselves. The paradox resolved itself — a paradox cannot sustain itself without input. You gave it none.
The self-other inversion is reversed. You reversed the reversal — healed yourself, attacked the enemy. The lake could not handle a double inversion. The spirits are gone.
The Hollow destroyed themselves with your identity. They fought as you — and your strength was too much for them to carry. They burned out. The lake is clear.
The Elite Reflection is disproven. You created — and a reflection can only copy. The original creates. The reflection imitates. You are the original because you made something new.
defeat: Withdraw. The identity-inversion was too strong. Return without attacking — let the paradox resolve itself.
The self-other inversion held. Return with double reversal — heal yourself, attack the enemy.
The Hollow were too good at being you. Return — let them fight themselves. Your strength will burn them out.
The Reflection's claim held. Return with creation — a reflection can only copy. Create something new.
codex: Elite Mirror Lake missions escalate the inversion to identity itself. The deity's reflection claims to be the original, and the Mirror agrees. The deity must prove primacy through the one thing a reflection cannot do: create. Reflections copy. Originals create. The deity who makes something new — something no reflection could imitate — proves they are the original. This is the Elite Kami trial of originality: you are not what you reflect. You are what you create.

intro: Elite Hidden Shrine Archive. The Gate's containment protocol is not just inward-facing mirrors — it is self-reinforcing mirrors. The mirrors reflect each other, creating an infinite loop of self-observation. Break the loop.
Elite archive-keepers that reflect attacks through infinite mirror-chains. Your force bounces between mirrors forever. Do not attack — the loop will never end.
Elite containment constructs that maintain the infinite self-observation loop. The deity is trapped watching themselves watching themselves. Break the loop by looking away.
The Elite Archive Mirror with infinite recursion. It shows the deity watching the deity watching the deity — forever. The only escape is to close your eyes and walk.
enemy: Infinite mirror-chain keepers. They reflect attacks through endless mirror loops. Your force bounces forever. Do not attack — walk through.
Self-reinforcing containment mirrors. They reflect each other, creating infinite self-observation. The deity is trapped in the loop. Break it by not looking.
Elite constructs maintaining the recursion. They enforce self-observation — the deity must watch themselves. Close your eyes. They cannot enforce what you refuse to do.
The Elite Archive Mirror with infinite recursion. The deity watching the deity, forever. Close your eyes and walk. The loop requires observation. Without it, the loop dies.
mid: The mirror-chains reflect attacks infinitely. Do not attack. Walk through — the mirrors cannot reflect what does not strike. The chain dies without input.
The self-observation loop traps you. Break it by not looking. Close your eyes. The loop requires observation. Without it, the loop is just glass.
The constructs enforce self-observation. They cannot enforce what you refuse to do. Close your eyes and walk. They have no power over the blind.
The infinite recursion requires observation. Close your eyes. The loop dies without the observer. Walk forward blind. The archive is in the dark, not the light.
victory: The infinite mirror-chain is broken. You walked through without attacking. The chain died without input. The mirrors are just glass — and glass does not fight.
The self-observation loop is shattered. You closed your eyes and walked. The loop died without the observer. The archive is open in the dark.
The containment constructs are gone. They could not enforce what you refused to do. The blind walk through mirrors. The sighted are trapped by them.

The Elite Archive Mirror is dark. The infinite recursion died without observation. You walked forward blind and found the truth in the dark. The containment protocol is broken. The Kami can close their eyes and walk out.
defeat: Withdraw. The mirror-chain was infinite. Return without attacking — walk through.
The self-observation loop trapped you. Return with closed eyes — the loop dies without the observer.
The constructs enforced observation. Return blind — they cannot enforce what you refuse to do.
The recursion held you. Return with closed eyes — the loop dies without observation. Walk forward blind.
codex: Elite Hidden Shrine Archive missions reveal the Gate's deepest containment mechanism: infinite mirror recursion. The mirrors reflect each other, creating an endless loop of self-observation. The deity is trapped watching themselves watching themselves, forever. The only escape is to close their eyes and walk — the loop requires observation. Without the observer, the loop is just glass. This is the Elite Kami trial of liberation: the cage was not the mirrors. The cage was the looking. Stop looking. Walk out.

intro: Elite False Mirror Queen. She now reflects not just the deity but the deity's freedom. She is the deity un-caged, and she claims that the un-caged version is still her. Fight your own liberation.
The Elite Queen creates reflections of everyone the deity has freed — the allies, the archived truth, the broken mirrors. She uses the deity's victories as weapons. Win without using your past.

The Elite Queen and the Elite Mirror are one. She defines reality not just through reflection but through freedom — she claims that to be free of the Mirror is still to be defined by the Mirror. Exist without definition.

Final Elite confrontation. The Queen claims that even breaking free is a Mirror-authorized action — the Mirror planned for liberation. Prove that freedom is not a plan. Exist outside the Mirror's design.
enemy: The Elite Queen reflecting the deity's freedom. She is the un-caged deity — and she claims the un-caged version is still hers. Fight your own liberation without rejecting it.
Reflected allies, freed truth, broken mirrors — all used as weapons. Your victories turned against you. Win without relying on your past. Fight with your present.
The Elite Queen defining reality through freedom itself. She claims that being free of the Mirror is still being defined by the Mirror. Exist without any definition.

codex: The Elite False Mirror Queen campaign is the culmination of the Kami arc. The Queen's final claim — that even liberation is a Mirror-authorized action — is the deepest cage of all: the cage that makes the caged believe their escape was planned. The deity's victory is to exist outside all definition: neither caged nor free, neither defined by the Mirror nor defined against it. Simply being. The Mirror cannot contain, liberate, or reflect what exists without definition. The Kami campaign's central lesson: existence without definition cannot be contained. The deity who is neither caged nor free — who simply is — has transcended the Mirror entirely. And the Mirror, for the first time, has nothing to reflect.
